name: UT-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Post-redistricting district leans strongly Democratic (D+12 PVI)
Prediction markets price McAdams at 96% on both Kalshi and Polymarket
McAdams has a massive financial edge: $2.3M raised plus $2.7M outside support vs. minimal Republican spending
model.rationale: The fundamentals point decisively to Democrats after redistricting, and markets on two platforms price McAdams near-certain. His overwhelming fundraising and outside-spending advantage over Riley Owen reinforces a Safe D rating with a margin near the fundamentals estimate.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Owen consolidating Republicans and moderate swing voters, or a major outside-spending surge against McAdams, could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; fundamentals point clearly one way (post-redistricting), so it is treated as safe for that party.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Utah's first district became substantially more Democratic after redistricting, and Ben McAdams enters the open-seat race as a heavy favorite. He has raised over $2.2 million and benefits from roughly $2.7 million in outside support, while Republican Riley Owen has raised only about $133,000 with almost no cash on hand and no outside spending on either side. Independent and Libertarian candidates appear on the ballot but lack resources.

With no public general-election polling, the forecast rests on district fundamentals and market pricing, both of which point the same direction. Kalshi and Polymarket each give McAdams a 96 percent win probability. The expected margin is around 21 points, with meaningful uncertainty given the absence of polls, but the race is rated Safe Democratic.
